what_it_does: Serverless computing is a cloud model where customers run short-lived functions on demand and pay only for what they use, with the cloud provider managing all the underlying hardware. Running AI inference (asking a trained model for predictions) in this model is attractive but wasteful: the provider must pre-allocate a fixed slice of a graphics processor (GPU) to each function, and because demand fluctuates, anywhere from 15% to 94% of each GPU's capacity sits unused at any moment — a problem called fragmentation. Dilu tackles this with what it calls 'introspective elasticity': the ability to both stretch or shrink the GPU resources assigned to a single running function (adjusting vertically, like upgrading RAM in a computer while it runs) and to add or remove additional copies of the function (scaling horizontally, like opening more checkout lanes). The system profiles each AI function to understand whether it is more sensitive to compute power or memory capacity, then uses that knowledge to slot compatible functions into the gaps left by others, filling otherwise wasted GPU space while keeping response times within promised limits.
